Counts are 17/17/17/16 across ACT_1..ACT_4, inside episode_spec's figure_beats_per_act [13,17]; HOOK 2 and ENDING 2; 71 cards in total. EVERY number on a `stat` card is a number the narration speaks -- 412, 3, 15, 41, 8, 95, 225, 253, 317, 420, 144, 24, 30, 71, 90, 102, 1000, 33, 400, 40, 2, 100 -- and every `value` is an int, so nothing can render as NaN. _declared_values.ranges_are_never_stats: The two ranges in this episode are the reported occupancy (440 to 458, ST-101) and the share who went for the front entrance (56 to 66 per cent, ST-401). Both live in a `kinetic` card's `lines` as text. A range cannot be a `stat` value -- a string there renders NaN in 100-pixel type (EP76 morandi, five cards).
_declared_values.no_OP_section: episode_spec's section_vocabulary lists OP, but narration_index has no OP chunks -- the brand opening is an overlay on the HOOK, not a spoken section. A card there would have no window to live in.
_declared_values.quarantine: Nothing on screen touches charges, pleas, sentences or convictions: the Rhode Island court record is source S3 in the facts ledger and has NOT been opened (episode_spec forbidden_claims). No card says the owners knew the foam was flammable, that the fire department was slow, that the crowd panicked, or that everyone could have escaped. The occupancy range is labelled as REPORTED and attributed to news media and the Attorney General's office, never stated as an established count -- and the NIST video count of 144 is paired with NIST's own statement that the sequence cannot be timed. The counterfactuals in ACT_4 are NIST's own, attributed as theirs. The 95-per-cent figure NIST's public summary gives for fatalities attributable to inability to evacuate does not appear anywhere; it was not located in Volume 1. No name of any person who died appears. The `stat` card carrying 95 is the fuel-load share (ST-006), which is a different fact and is labelled as such.
